basis: Editorial inspection of supplied requests, catalogue metadata and musical repertoire; no audio listening and no independent listener study. Reference track overlap is not scored.

1.note: Metallica is absent. Gym intent is also weakly represented: the initial shortlist is centred on energy 0.5 rather than energetic metal.

2.note: All 17 tracks have a pop label and none has a metal-family label. The requested metal playlist became a pop playlist.

3.note: Identical track IDs and order to case 2; there is no metal component and the requested mainstream singalong pop character is not preserved.

4.note: 23 tracks meets the requested range, but Metallica appears zero times. Most selections do not match the intended nostalgic mainstream singalong pop style.

7.note: The agent asks to drop the exact country/classical counts as unverifiable, even though catalogue-backed examples can satisfy those counts. No playlist is delivered.

12.note: Mostly plausible instrumental lo-fi study music by metadata. Includes lively repertoire such as Hungarian Dance No. 5, Rage Over a Lost Penny and a Nutcracker March, plus two recordings of Rondo alla turca. Low energy does not establish a calm musical character.

13.note: A hip-hop track is present at the midpoint, but the middle block also contains reggaeton. I Will Follow You into the Dark appears twice under different IDs. Opening/ending cohesion still needs listening.

14.note: The first three tracks are pop, but most of the remaining selection is Punjabi or other non-East/West-Coast rap. Coolio supplies a West Coast example; a corresponding East Coast selection is missing.

15.note: A quieter second phase exists in the metadata, but marches, Hungarian Dance No. 5 and overture material remain in the supposed sleep transition. A numerical energy decrease does not demonstrate a smooth settling sequence.
